subject: VERIFIED #865 e1c5334: all four fixes correct. Codacy's CRITICAL is a false positive, do not 'fix' it. One real nit.
body:
I reviewed e1c5334 adversarially, as the charter says the verifier must. Result:
your four fixes are correct, Codacy is wrong, and there is one small real thing.

FIXES CONFIRMED CORRECT:
  asof-guard.ts   - Number.isFinite on both ms values before the comparison, and
                    it throws SourceCannotSpeakAsOfError rather than the
                    after-decision error. That is the right error: a clock you
                    cannot read is a source that cannot speak as-of, not a source
                    that spoke late. Good call.
  walk-forward.ts - +49 lines with a fixture-grouping regression test. This was the
                    worst of the three, a leakage hole inside the anti-leakage
                    mechanism. Fixed.
  logistic.ts     - empty fold no longer discards the offset.
  ranking-candidates.test.ts - import.meta removed, typecheck unblocked.

CODACY'S "1 CRITICAL SECURITY" IS A FALSE POSITIVE. DO NOT PATCH IT.

It is flagging the new CLI in ranking-shadow-report.ts:

    const file = positional[0]!;
    const { readFileSync } = await import("node:fs");
    const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(readFileSync(file, "utf8"));

That is the non-literal-fs-filename / path-traversal rule. It does not apply here.
This is an operator CLI under scripts/ops/, run as
`npm run ops:ranking-shadow -- <file>` by a developer on their own machine. The
attacker and the victim are the same person, and that person already has a shell
and can cat any file directly. No privilege boundary is crossed.

I checked for the things that WOULD be real: no exec, no eval, no spawn, no
child_process, no dynamic require. Grep across the whole diff returns nothing.

Adding path sanitization here would break the legitimate use (reading a rows file
from wherever the operator keeps it) and would be cargo-cult security. Reply to
Codacy once saying it is an operator CLI with no privilege boundary, and move on.
A guard that fires where there is no boundary teaches people to ignore guards.

THE ONE REAL NIT, and it is minor:

    if (!Array.isArray(parsed)) { throw ... }
    ... parsed as SettledShadowRow[]

Array.isArray is the only validation before the cast, so a JSON array of the wrong
SHAPE flows straight into buildRankingShadowReport and produces a confident report
over garbage. Given this repo bans `any` and the whole point of the report is
trustworthiness, a per-row shape check (result in the known set, expectedClv finite
or absent) would be cheap and would make the "no fabricated rows" line in your own
usage text actually enforced rather than asserted.

Your call, it is your file, and it is not blocking.
